explanation: Store inserted words in a set. Exact search tests set membership; prefix search scans stored words until one begins with the requested prefix. This implements the callable behavior without building character-trie nodes.
timeComplexity: Expected O(L) insertion/exact search including hashing a length-L word. Prefix search scans up to W words with up to P character comparisons each: O(W(P+1)).
spaceComplexity: O(S+W) stored content/references for W distinct words of total length S; prefix scanning itself needs constant extra state. JavaScript spreads the set into an O(W) temporary array for each prefix query.
attribution: Original repository-authored Blind75 JavaScript algorithm, promoted from the validated correct fixtures. Collection membership follows Crackr; no external solution service is used.
correctness: The set contains exactly the distinct inserted words, so membership answers complete-word search. A prefix query succeeds exactly when at least one stored word starts with that prefix, which the scan tests directly. An empty set therefore rejects even an empty prefix; once any word is stored its empty prefix matches.
walkthrough: The empty set makes startsWith("") false. Insert "mint", creating {mint}; startsWith("mi") finds that word, while search("mi") is false. Insert "mi" and exact search becomes true. Query outputs are [false,true,false,true]. The arrays describe calls on one instance in order; expected contains only Search/StartsWith boolean results, omitting Insert returns.
edgeCases: Prefix search and exact search are different operations.
Reinserting the same word does not duplicate it.
The empty prefix is false before any insertion.
